previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted following a fall from his wheelchair four days prior, resulting in a right intertrochanteric femur fracture and right tibia/fibula fracture. Given his baseline paraplegia and comorbidities, non-operative management with bracing was chosen over surgery. He received closed reduction in the emergency department, with stable alignment confirmed on follow-up imaging. His pain was well controlled, and he engaged in physical therapy while in the hospital. A concurrent urinary tract infection was treated with amoxicillin-clavulanate. He remained neurologically stable, with no complications during his stay. He was discharged home with home health services, a new wheelchair, and detailed instructions for non-weight-bearing status, skin care, anticoagulation, and medication management.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ man with paraplegia ___ MVA in ___, chronic kidney 
disease, chronic indwelling foley with recurrent uriny tract 
infections, seizure disorder, polysubstance abuse, and 
hypertension admitted with hematuria and chills.  
.  
#HEMATURIA AND CHILLS/URINARY TRACT INFECTION: Patient presented 
with hematuria and chills; afebrile without any other evidence 
of SIRS on admission and throughout hospitalization. His 
urinalysis showed many bacteria/yeast, >182 WBCs, large 
leukocytes. Therefore, UTI was the most  likely diagnosis. 
Nephrolithiasis was considered, but CT ___ showed no 
stones. Scrotal U/S was negative and GC/chlamydia also found 
negative making epididymo-orchitis unlikely as well. Patient was 
initially covered empirically for UTI with Cefepime, and 
symptoms improved. UCx grew mixed bacterial flora c/w fecal 
contamination. However, out of high concern that one of these 
organisms could represent UTI pathogen and not only contaminant, 
cultures were plated out and ultimately grew E. coli, Klebsiella 
pneumoniae and yeast spp sensitive to cefepime and ceftriaxone. 
Patient was therefore transitioned to PO cefpodoxime to complete 
14 day antibiotic course (last day ___. 
.  
#NAUSEA/VOMITING/Possible pancreatitis: On HD#4, patient 
developed new nausea and had large-volume guaiac negative 
emesis, which resolved rapidly. He reports that this occurs 
frequently at home. Amylase and lipase were both found elevated 
to 101. RUQ ultrasound showed dilated common bile duct but no 
visualized gallstones. Triglycerides elevated to 248 on last 
check (___). Patient denies frequent EtOH use, but drugs 
(including opiates, of which he takes high doses) can also cause 
pancreatitis. As pt also reported severe constipation, 
considered SBO, but abdominal U/S did not show evidence of this. 
Patient's symptoms improved within one day with home pain meds, 
zofran and NPO (quickly advanced back to regular diet). He will 
follow up with GI as outpatient to further explore question of 
chronic pancreatitis.  
.  
# TESTICULAR PAIN: patient had e/o fungal infection, likely 
candidiasis, in his scrotal region on exam. Ruled out 
epididymitis, orchitis, and nephrolithiasis as etiologies of 
testicular pain via imaging per above. GC/chlamydia were 
negative. Patient received topical miconazole powder TID, and 
scrotum was kept clean and dry. He will continue miconazole 
until symptoms resolve. Symptoms improved over the course of the 
hospitalization. 
.  
# CONSTIPATION: 
pt reported significant constipation on ___, unsure if passing 
gas. KUB showed e/o possible fecal impaction, but no e/o SBO or 
ileus. Constipation likely ___ narcotic medications and being 
sedentary. Patient refused all oral constipation meds, so 
instead received Bisacodyl suppositories and tap water enema 
with resolution of constipation. 
.  
#Chronic kidney disease: Baseline Cr ranged from 2.3 to 3.2 over 
last year. Creatinine was 3.2 on admission; improved back to 2.4 
after IV fluids. Urine studies unremarkable. Likely prerenal 
insufficiency secondary to infection. 
.  
#SOMNOLENCE: Pt was very lethargic and only AAOx2 on admission. 
Urine tox was positive for cocaine, as well as benzos and 
opiates (which he is prescribed). Drug intoxication or 
withdrawal were likely etiology of his altered mental status. 
Neuro exam was nonfocal. He returned to his baseline normal 
mental status over the next couple of days. His home alprazolam 
and zolpidem were held. Alprazolam was discontinued on discharge 
from hospital. 
.  
# LOW BACK PAIN: Pt has been taking oxycodone 60mg TID (not 
oxycontin due to insurance coverage issues) as well as percocet 
for pain. Home meds were continued.

#Disposition: 
Patient was discharged home with PCP and outpatient GI follow 
up.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with paraplegia, intermittent marijuana use,
chronic Foley catheter, and left hip osteomyelitis.  Presents with hematuria,
right flank pain, and positive urinalysis.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  Helical MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases through the
greater trochanters without intravenous contrast, due to the patient's renal
failure.  5-mm axial, coronal, and sagittal multiplanar reformats were
generated.

FINDINGS:  Note is made of bilateral gynecomastia.  There is atelectasis at
the lung bases.  No pleural effusions are present.  Heart is normal in size,
without pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:  Kidneys are markedly atrophic, with cortical thinning and
lobulation.  There is increased fullness of the bilateral collecting systems,
suggestive of reflux.  No obstructing stones or masses are identified, and
there is no transition point compatible with obstruction.  The adrenals are
normal.  

The liver, gallbladder, and pancreas are unremarkable on this non-contrast
examination.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary ductal dilation. 
Spleen is normal in size.  Note is made of an accessory splenule at the
splenic hilum.

The stomach and small bowel are normal.  Prominent celiac and superior
paraaortic nodes measure 8-13 mm.

PELVIS:  Foley catheter is present in a partially collapsed bladder, with
chronic moderate circumferential wall thickening.  The prostate and seminal
vesicles are unremarkable.  

The appendix, colon, and rectum are normal.  Cluster of lymph nodes in the
right lower quadrant measure 8-12 mm.  

There is a small fat-containing right inguinal hernia.  Bilateral inguinal
lymph nodes measure up to 10 mm.  

Chronic compression deformity of T12 shows 60% loss of anterior height and
near-complete obliteration of the T11-12 interspace.  Laminectomy and
posterior fusion changes are seen from T9 through L2, with pedicle screws at
the L1 and L2 levels.  Hardware appears well seated, without periprosthetic
lucency or fracture.  

The pelvis has a dysmorphic appearance.  Bone graft donor site is noted in the
left ilium.  There is a chronic left hip effusion, with heterogeneous joint
fluid and fat stranding.  Continued superoposterior dislocation of the left
femoral head, with coxa magna/breva and pseudoarthrosis along the left iliac
wing.  There is periarticular heterotopic ossification.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Renal atrophy and prominent collecting systems, suggestive of reflux. 
Limited detection of pyelonephritis or renal abscess without intravenous
contrast.
2.  Bladder wall thickening, indicating chronic inflammation or infection.
3.  Chronic left hip effusion and pseudoarthrosis.

DLP:  562.66 mGy-cm.

INDICATION:  Patient with paraplegia and chronic indwelling Foley catheter,
now with pyuria, hematuria and chills.  Assess for epididymitis or orchitis.

COMPARISON:  None available.

FINDINGS:

The right testicle measures 3.7 x 2.9 x 2.2 cm and left testicle measures 2.1
x 2.6 x 2 cm.  The testicles are normal in echotexture and vascularity.  The
epididymides are unremarkable without hyperemia.  Small amount of complex
hydrocele with internal echoes is seen in the left hemiscrotum.

IMPRESSION:

Small complex left-sided hydrocele, may represent sequela of prior
inflammatory process; however, there is no evidence of acute epididymitis or
orchitis.
